title: Yusuf in one sitting, part two
hook: Surah 12:58–111, from the brothers to the fulfilled dream
tomorrow: a few young men run for a cave. what do they pray at its mouth?

segments.voice: Yesterday, part one: the dream, the well, the shirt, the storehouses, and Jordan's Joseph beside Amira's Yusuf. The line: the best of stories. This week ran from the Opening to here, and it ends with brothers at a door.
screen: `THE BEST OF STORIES.` → `BROTHERS AT A DOOR.`

segments.voice: Hana is coming over tonight to see Dadi. It's the first time since the bangles, and Amira has rehearsed three openings in the shower. In the surah, the brothers walk into Egypt hungry, asking for grain, and stand in front of the man they threw into a well. He knows them at once. They have no idea who he is. He has the storehouses, the power, every reason. So what does he do?
screen: `HANA IS COMING OVER.` → `HE KNOWS THEM. THEY DON'T KNOW HIM.` → `EVERY REASON.`

segments.voice: He feeds them first. He asks them to bring the youngest brother, and when they do, a royal cup turns up in the youngest's bag, and the story tightens. Back home, Ya'qub has wept until his eyes went white with grief, and he still sends his sons out with a command not to despair of Allah's mercy. They return to Yusuf, humbled, and he asks them if they know what they did to Yusuf. Then, in Pickthall's words: "I am Joseph and this is my brother." They confess. And he says: no blame on you today; may Allah forgive you. His shirt is laid on his father's face, and Ya'qub sees again. The whole family bows, and Yusuf says the dream from the start has come true. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: tradition says that when the Prophet, peace be upon him, entered Mecca, before the people who had driven him out, he gave them Yusuf's words. No blame on you today. The best of stories, finished in mercy.
screen: `HE FEEDS THEM FIRST.` · `I AM JOSEPH AND THIS IS MY BROTHER.` · `THE SHIRT, AND THE SIGHT.` · `THE DREAM COMES TRUE.` · then, large: `NO BLAME ON YOU TODAY.`

segments.voice: Think of one person you owe a first word to, the way Yusuf spoke first. Type the opening line of that message on your phone, just one line, and hold it in your hand for the sit. Sending it is a choice for later.
screen: `ONE FIRST WORD.` · `TYPE ONE LINE. HOLD IT.`

segments.voice: Yusuf in one sitting: the whole surah, from a boy's dream to a family bowing, finished in mercy.
For the week's end: no blame on you today, said by the one who could have blamed. Two weeks, whole.

howItsDone: Muslims read Surah Yusuf whole, and 'no blame on you today', la tathriba 'alaykum al-yawm, is quoted when a wrong is forgiven without reproach.

match.prompt: part two of the story — tap the pairs.
pairs: come to Egypt hungry, for grain

myth: Yusuf took his revenge on his brothers before forgiving them
he fed them, tested them, and at the reveal said: no blame on you today; may Allah forgive you.
in the Qur'an, Yusuf's shirt brings back his father's sight
laid on Ya'qub's face, it restores his sight, and the family comes to Egypt.

fork.setup: a guy who once stole from your dad's coffee shop comes back, broke, asking for work. your dad asks what you think. what does Yusuf's part two model?
options: meet him without shaming him, and look at what's right now.
make him pay back every dollar first; then the past is clear.
turn him away; forgiving means you never have to see him.
fork.reveal: Yusuf held every card and said no blame on you today. the surah doesn't say pretend nothing happened; it says don't reproach.

original.note: Arabic: no blame on you today, Yusuf's words to his brothers in 12:92.

trapdoor: what you thought: a happy ending where everyone hugs.
what it means: the one with all the power chooses mercy without reproach, and the dream from the start comes true.
what a scholar hears: 12:92 la tathriba 'alaykum al-yawm; the shirt in 12:93–96; the dream fulfilled in 12:100; Mecca in the sira.
guess: Surah Yusuf read whole, ending in forgiveness
a fast kept in memory of Yusuf's years in prison
the Bible's Joseph chapters read aloud at a mosque

chat.says: hana's here for dadi in an hour. i want to fix the bangle thing. wait for HER to start?
options: Start. Yusuf could have punished and spoke first: no blame on you today.
Skip the talk. Forgiving means acting like none of it ever happened.
Give her the bangles. Fixing it means handing over what she wanted.
chat.meaning: Yusuf held all the power and chose mercy without reproach: 'no blame on you today; may Allah forgive you.'

Yusuf.meaning: a prophet in the Qur'an; Joseph in the Bible

Ya'qub.meaning: Yusuf's father, a prophet; Jacob in the Bible

Mecca.meaning: the Prophet's birthplace, the city of the Ka'bah

sources.quoted: I am Joseph and this is my brother.

sources.ref: Qur'an 12:58–111 (the brothers come for grain; the youngest brother; the cup; Ya'qub's grief and 'despair not of the Spirit of Allah' (12:87); the reveal; 'no blame on you today' (12:92); the shirt and the sight (12:93–96); the dream fulfilled (12:100))
Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (as transmitted by Ibn Hisham), on the conquest of Mecca: 'no blame on you today'
